newsitem.title: POLAND: NBP pulls rug from under zloty, T/N depos rise.
newsitem.headline: NBP pulls rug from under zloty, T/N depos rise.

text.p: A series of central bank currency-buying interventions pulled the rug from under the zloty, sinking it more than 2.5 groszes against the dollar and more than one grosz down against the mark, dealers said.
The zloty closed at 3.1420/60 against the dollar and 1.8210/30 against the mark, down from 3.1200/10 and 1.8082/87 zlotys respectively on Wednesday.
It closed at 2.55/2.47 percent from the trading band centre, down from 3.23/3.13 percent at the opening after the National Bank of Poland bought an estimated $200 million.
"The zloty found support at 2.5 percent from the parity rate as foreign inflows partly neutralised NBP interventions," said Mateusz Bieniek of Societe Generale in Warsaw.

Dealers said the central bank currency buying, which knocked the zloty down from early highs of 3.2 percent from the dollar parity rate, sparked a frenzy of Polish T-bill purchases by foreign investors and, in turn, more interventions.
"Foreign investors were immediately attracted to Polish paper as the zloty started falling on the intervetions," said Witold Wozniak of Deutsche Bank Polska SA.

On the money market overnight rates held relatively flat at 21.75/22.10 percent while tomorrow/next rates rose 21.80/22.00 pct after a 565 million zloty reverse repo and a 92 million zloty NBP-bill sale which reduced the market's liquidity.
The average yield of the 91-day rose to 22.19 percent from 22.17 percent at the last tender of the bnds while the maximum yield returned to its previous level of 22.20 percent from 22.18 yesterday.
The finance ministry raised the minimum price of its 12-percent five-year assimilated bonds, due June 12, 2001, to 80.76 from 80.55 percent at the last tender on March 20.
It sold 182 million zlotys worth of the paper against a 231 million zloty demand at the 300 million zloty auction.
